classification.acceptable_short_alias: coarse-input countermodel for the adjacent-small-mismatch route
nearest_prior_work: Erdos (1988), p. 103, is the primary statement of the fixed dyadic prime series and makes clear that even the k=1 case was unresolved.

Erdos and Pomerance (1978), section 7, provide a genuinely arithmetic adjacent dyadic-series irrationality theorem whose proof uses eventual binary periodicity plus number-theoretic structure; this is a useful contrast to the present deliberately non-arithmetic orbit.
The closed-form recurrence verification itself is routine finite-difference algebra and does not warrant a standalone novelty claim.
classification.attribution: Attribute the target problem and its difficulty to Erdos's 1988 problem statement. Describe the local asset as an authored Lean-checked stress test which rules out a specified proof route under specified coarse assumptions, not as prior work on prime-gap distribution.
classification.mathematical_interest: Low theorem depth but high diagnostic precision: one exact family simultaneously satisfies positivity, parity, strict polynomial growth, unboundedness, nonperiodicity, and rational tail integrality while avoiding every adjacent plus-or-minus-two event.
classification.reusable_scope: Affine radix-tail arguments in which an irrationality producer is claimed from qualitative growth or recurrence properties alone. A candidate proof should first be tested against explicit rational polynomial orbits satisfying those same coarse properties.
classification.why_it_matters: It prevents additional generic gap-growth lemmas from being misreported as progress on #251. To escape the countermodel, a proof must consume a property of actual consecutive primes, a stronger multi-offset producer, or a separate theorem excluding rational prime-tail orbits.

primary_sources.author: Paul Erdos and Carl Pomerance
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Section 7, printed p. 320: irrationality of a binary series encoding whether P(n)>P(n+1), proved from eventual periodicity, Polya's finiteness theorem, and the positive-density result of section 6.

primary_sources.does_not_support: It is not about the nth-prime numerator series, consecutive-prime gaps, or the polynomial orbit in the local card.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: Given a chosen polynomial state T_n, defining g_(n+1)=2T_n-T_(n+1) automatically manufactures a polynomial forcing word for the affine dyadic-tail recurrence. Direct expansion checks all displayed properties here.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The useful work is hypothesis alignment: one orbit is certified to meet every named coarse property while also being integral and having no adjacent plus-or-minus-two digit event.
mechanism_comparison.contrast_with_arithmetic_prior_work: The Erdos-Pomerance dyadic theorem succeeds because eventual periodicity conflicts with a number-theoretic property of its actual arithmetic digit sequence. The polynomial orbit demonstrates why qualitative growth of a surrogate word cannot replace such input for #251.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The construction retires only recurrence-plus-coarse-growth proofs of the h=1 producer. It neither challenges the producer for actual prime gaps nor rules out larger offsets, other digit events, or direct irrationality arguments.
